hypotheses.justification: The result holds for arbitrary s. Let t := toMeasurable volume s, which is measurable (hence null-measurable) and contains s (subset_toMeasurable). Since volume on the finite-dimensional inner product space U is s-finite (it is an add Haar measure, hence σ-finite), Measure.restrict_toMeasurable_of_sfinite (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Typeclasses/SFinite.lean) gives volume.restrict t = volume.restrict s. As IntegrableOn g s is Integrable g (volume.restrict s), hint for s transfers verbatim to IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ (fderiv ℝ f x).normDet) t. Applying the existing proof (ae_summable_fiber with hs instantiated at t, then Finite.of_summable_const) to t gives ∀ᵐ y ∂μHE[finrank ℝ U], (t ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}).Finite. Then s ∩ f ⁻¹' {y} ⊆ t ∩ f ⁻¹' {y} gives finiteness for s via Set.Finite.subset. So the statement stays true and provable after deleting hs. I could not run Lean, so this proof sketch is unchecked.
